input.quote: 12.3 Additional Termination Rights by AbbVie. AbbVie may terminate this Agreement in its entirety, or on a country or other jurisdiction -by-country or other jurisdiction basis, for any or no reason, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Harpoon.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 gives us (AbbVie, as Customer) an unconditional at-will termination right — in whole or country-by-country, "for any or no reason" — on ninety (90) days' prior written notice, which sits squarely within the fallback range of 60–90 days' notice. No early-termination or exit fee is imposed for exercising Section 12.3: the consequences provisions (12.6.1, 12.7, 12.8, 12.10) address reversion of rights, sell-off of inventory and accrued/surviving payment obligations only, so the fallback cap of three months' fees is satisfied a fortiori. On the counterparty side, Harpoon's termination rights are limited to uncured material breach (12.2.1/12.2.2) and insolvency (12.4); Harpoon has no convenience right at all, which is better than the fallback (end-of-term only on 90 days' notice) and matches the preferred position that Vendor may not walk away mid-term. The clause therefore meets the fallback on its material terms and we do not redline it. Noted short of preferred only in the minor respects that our notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; given the upfront and milestone payments here are expressly non-refundable as part of the negotiated economics, we would raise refund language only if reopening Article 6.
